listings.name: Flinders Street Station
listings.content: The defining landmark of Melbourne, this colonial-era railway station was designed in an 1899 competition. The station's front steps, below a row of clocks announcing train departure times, are a popular meeting point for locals. It is the busiest suburban station in the Southern Hemisphere. Although grand from the outside, the interior has become dilapidated over the years and many rooms including the ballroom are closed to the public. A restoration project began in 2015 and further works were announced in 2018.

listings.name: Government House
listings.content: The official residence of the Governor of Victoria. The house opened in 1876 as the official residence of the Governor-General of Australia, before the capital moved to Canberra. The house is modelled to some extent on Queen Victoria's Osborne House, in Cowes, England. Combined tours with La Trobe's Cottage must be booked two weeks in advance. Free garden tours on third Thursday of the month, limited to 10 people so book well in advance. Visit on the Open Day on Australia Day (26 January).

listings.name: Governor La Trobe's Cottage
listings.content: A prefabricated cottage imported from England in 1839 for Victoria's first Lt. Governor, Charles Joseph La Trobe. The cottage has been rebuilt and relocated. The cottage and garden is run by the National Trust.
listings.address: Corner of Birdwood Avenue & Dallas Brooks Drive, The Domain

listings.name: Melbourne Town Hall
listings.content: Built in 1870, the city's town hall is grand and historic. 1 hour tours allow visitors to see the ornate Council chambers, the richly-carved Grand Organ and sit in the Lord Mayor's chair. Bookings recommended.

listings.name: Old Melbourne Gaol
listings.content: Built in 1841, it is now a penal museum, with a watch house and magistrate's court also on-site. Bushranger Ned Kelly was hanged here in 1880. The scaffold on which he and many others were hanged is displayed, as is Kelly’s death mask. There are other displays in many of the cells. Allow an hour or so for your visit.
listings.price: $30 adult, $25 concession, $17 child (5-15yrs), family tickets available (free for National Trust members and members of reciprical trusts overseas)

listings.name: Parliament House of Victoria
listings.content: Built between 1856 and 1879, the Australian federal parliament sat in this impressive building from 1901 to 1927 while Canberra was built. It now houses the state parliament. The majestic façade can be seen right down Bourke St. Tours of the assembly halls and libraries are conducted when parliament is not in session. Visitors are also welcome to sit in the public gallery when parliament is in session.

listings.name: Scots Church
listings.content: Gothic church built in 1873, the first Presbyterian house of worship in the city.

listings.name: Shrine of Remembrance
listings.content: War memorial in classical style opened in 1934. The memorial was designed so that the sun would shine on the word LOVE at 11AM on 11 November. Exhibition galleries under the memorial were added in 2014. A Last Post Service is held here every Sunday at 4.45pm to commemorate an important event in Australia's military history.

listings.name: State Library of Victoria
listings.content: Built in stages beginning in 1854, it has an impressive classical revival façade. Includes a good newspaper reading room, genealogy room and an art collection, as well as the fantastic La Trobe Reading Room and its huge dome. Bushranger Ned Kelly's armour is stored permanently on display, along with a variety of galleries and exhibitions. Internet terminals are provided for research only, not email, and usually need to be booked because of high demand. Coin-operated lockers are available just off the lobby, where large bags must be deposited before entry. Free Wi-Fi and guided tours are also available.

listings.name: St Michaels Uniting Church
listings.content: Romanesque-style church built in 1866.

listings.name: St Patrick’s Cathedral
listings.content: The original part of this Gothic Revival cathedral was built in the 1850s. It was consecrated in 1897 and the spires added in 1939. It is the largest and tallest church in Australia.

listings.name: St Paul's Cathedral
listings.content: Gothic-revival cathedral on the site of the colony's first church services in 1836.

listings.name: Crown Entertainment Complex
listings.content: A Las Vegas-style gambling palace (including the Crown Casino), also containing restaurants, upmarket boutiques, nightclubs, two hotel towers, a cinema complex and floorshows.

listings.name: Eureka Tower
listings.content: Contains the highest observation deck in the Southern Hemisphere on level 88, with panoramic views of the entirety of Melbourne. Only recommended in clear weather. Also offers an additional cost "Edge" experience whereby visitors are protruded outside of the building inside a glass-panelled cube.
listings.price: $18.50 adult, $14 concession, $10 child (4-16yrs) and various family tickets. Discounted price for additional same-day visit at nighttime

listings.name: Federation Square
listings.content: The city's most popular meeting place. The striking architecture of its buildings create a nice backdrop to this open plaza, directly opposite Flinders Street Station. There are usually live, free performances from various groups, along with coverage of major sporting and cultural events on the huge television. A number of museums and organisations call the site home, as well as Melbourne's major visitor information centre in the 'shard' building.

listings.name: Melbourne Aquarium
listings.content: Home to over 10,000 aquatic creatures, there are four distinct areas of the aquarium dedicated to Antarctica, seahorses, the rainforest and the ocean, the latter of which includes a glass walk-through experience. Shark diving and animal feeding available.
listings.price: $35 adult, $21.50 child (4-15 yr), $29 concession, $92 family (2 adult+2 children); discounts online
listings.address: Cnr Flinders St and Kings Way

listings.name: ACDC Lane
listings.content: Formerly Corporation Lane, this alley was renamed in 2004 in honour of the world-famous Australian rock band. The laneway's sign is a nice photo opportunity for fans, plus it's located in the bar and rock district of the city.

listings.name: Hosier Lane
listings.content: If you want to sample street art, head for this little lane full of ever-evolving, colourful graffiti from end to end.

listings.name: Australian Centre for the Moving Image
listings.content: A museum, gallery and collection of cinemas dedicated to film, TV, video games, new media and art, both old and new. Regularly holds a number of interesting exhibitions.
listings.price: General entry free; charges apply for exhibitions

listings.name: The Ian Potter Centre
listings.content: Houses over 25,000 works of only Australian art, including paintings, sculptures, photography and fashion. Famous artists such as Frederick McCubbin and Sidney Nolan are on display, along with a fine collection of Indigenous art.

listings.name: National Gallery of Victoria
listings.content: The premier venue for international fine art exhibitions in Melbourne, with a permanent collection and international collections. A must-see for art lovers.

listings.name: Arts Centre Melbourne
listings.content: The Arts Centre Melbourne is home to the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra, the Australian Ballet, Opera Australia and the Melbourne Theatre Company. It has a variety of performance venues, exhibition spaces, bars and restaurants. On Sundays, it hosts an Artisans' Market.

listings.name: Koorie Heritage Trust
listings.content: Showcases contemporary art from Victorian First Peoples.

listings.name: ANZ Banking Museum
listings.content: Housed in the late-19th century Gothic Revival ANZ Bank building, it walks through the history of Australian banking from Indigenous bartering economies to finance of the future.

listings.name: Chinese Museum
listings.content: Situated in the midst of Chinatown, it documents and explains the history of Chinese immigrants in Australia. The 'millennium dragon' is on display, the largest Chinese dragon in the world, along with an interactive underground exhibit highlighting the goldfields. Also on-site is a free visitor centre and a gift shop. The museum runs walking tours of Chinatown by appointment ($10 per person).

listings.name: Fire Services Museum
listings.content: A largely niche museum, it is the largest fire service-related collection in Australia. Houses historical uniforms, vehicles, photos and other memorabilia.

listings.name: Immigration Museum
listings.content: Located in the restored Old Customs House, it covers customs and immigration history over the past 200 years. Details the stories and experiences of immigrations to Australia, both past and present.

listings.name: Old Treasury Building and Gold Museum
listings.content: Built in 1858 by a 19-year-old architect, it was the city’s first Italian Renaissance building and many consider that its elegance has not been surpassed by anything in Melbourne since. Contains displays on the history of Melbourne as well as the history of gold in Victoria, including the original gold vaults. Fun activities for children, including the chance to earn a novelty gold licence. The expansive Treasury Gardens behind the building are also worth a visit.

listings.name: Polly Woodside Maritime Museum
listings.content: A maritime museum based aboard the restored 1885 Belfast-built, three-masted, iron-hulled barque "Polly Woodside". Various kids activities available, including Pirate Sundays.

listings.name: Victoria Police Museum
listings.content: Displays with over 150 years of stories and of crime, justice, courage and forensic techniques. Includes some of the famous Kelly Gang's armour, the burnt out car used in the Russell Street Police HQ bombing and various records about famous gangland figures. Regular free exhibitions are on display.

listings.name: Alexandra Gardens
listings.content: Ornamental gardens laid out in 1904, on south bank of the Yarra River. There is a row of historic rowing boathouses on the river bank.

listings.name: Cooks' Cottage and Fitzroy Gardens
listings.content: Cooks' Cottage is the cottage that belonged to Captain James Cook’s parents and was transported from Yorkshire to Melbourne in 1934.

listings.name: Queen Victoria Gardens
listings.content: Features memorials to Queen Victoria and King Edward VII, sculptures and a floral clock of 7000 plants.

listings.name: Royal Botanic Gardens
listings.content: Recognised as one of the world’s finest botanic gardens, with over 10,000 species and 50,000 individual plants in the 38 hectare gardens.

listings.name: O'Brien Icehouse
listings.content: The largest ice recreation venue in the Southern Hemisphere, the O'Brien Icehouse allows visitors to skate around a large ice rink. There are free beginner classes on weekends and school holidays. It regularly holds public events such as dancing, games, and music parties.

listings.name: Aix
listings.content: Has a huge selection of mouth-wateringly good crepes.

listings.name: Manchester Press
listings.content: Specialty coffee, brekkie and bagels served in a light, vintage-chic cafe with eclectic decor.

listings.name: Axil
listings.content: Shop with barista who won 'Best Barista in the World' award in 2022, serving coffee, brekkie and light meals. Multiple locations across the CBD and Melbourne.

listings.name: Brunetti Oro Melbourne City
listings.content: Beautiful Italian cakes, desserts, and coffee. Available until late at night.

listings.name: Royal Stacks
listings.content: Royal Stacks is a mini homage to US burger chain, Shake Shack

listings.name: Simpsons Burgers
listings.content: Small shop serving a wide variety of burgers and sides, including chips and salads. Includes vegetarian options.

listings.name: Camy Shanghai Dumplings
listings.content: Chinese food in large servings, notable for its dumplings. Meals served with complimentary tea.

listings.name: Shanghai Street
listings.content: Cheap and cheerful dumplings, expect a queue as they don't take bookings

listings.name: Gaylords
listings.content: Kitschy ode to Bollywood in the heart of Chinatown.

listings.name: Tonka
listings.content: A ritzy, reservations-required Indian/Modern Australian fusion restaurant down one of Melbourne's most iconic laneways.

listings.name: Crossways
listings.content: Tasty lunch cafe with a 2-course vegetarian all-you-can-eat meal. May be possible to work 30 minutes for your meal.

listings.name: Gopals Pure Vegetarian
listings.content: Sister restaurant to Crossways.

listings.name: Om Vegetarian
listings.content: Cheap vegetarian and vegan buffet-style food which changes every day.

listings.name: Stalactites
listings.content: This Greek restaurant decorated with stalactites has delicious gyros and earthy meals.

listings.name: Hella Good
listings.content: Classic souvlaki place with two locations in the heart of Melbourne (the listed and another at Emporium Melbourne); open until midnight for late-night feasts.

listings.name: Il Mercato Centrale
listings.content: A recreation of food markets in Italy, this covered area features over 20 shops selling everything from gelato to panini.

listings.name: Brunetti Oro Flinders Lane
listings.content: A large Italian café, bar and restaurant serving a range of sweet and savoury food and drinks with lots of indoor and outdoor seating. One of two Brunetti Oro cafes in the city, the other being on Little Collins Street at Swanston Street.

listings.name: Romanello
listings.content: A small shop selling pizzas by the slice and freshly-made porchetta rolls next to the Queen Victoria Market.

listings.name: Cecconi's
listings.content: A long-standing stalwart of Melbourne's food scene, this is a fine dining restaurant featuring modern takes on Italian cuisine.

listings.name: Mama’s Bưởi
listings.content: Set in the modernised historic building of the Melbourne General Post Office, this Vietnamese restaurant offers quality meals at reasonable prices. As an indication, a set menu meal costs $25 each and includes a drink, entree and main, with four choices in each.

listings.name: Rozzis State Library
listings.content: A small cornerside New York-style pizza place. Prices tend to be a little on the higher end ($5–7/slice) but the slices are reasonably large and filling.

listings.name: Degraves Espresso Bar
listings.content: Tucked into a bluestone laneway near Flinders St Station, this outlet has long-held the title of Melbourne's best coffee. Hours: M–F 6:30AM–7:30PM, Sa Su 7:30AM-6:30PM.

listings.name: Brother Baba Budan
listings.content: Speciality coffee shop serving cakes in a quirky space with wood panelling and bar stools.

listings.name: Patricia Coffee Brewers
listings.content: Trendy, bare-bones, standing-room-only spot for artisanal coffee ground on-site, and small treats.
listings.address: Little Bourke St & Little William St

listings.name: Dukes Coffee Roasters
listings.content: Speciality outpost crafting home-grown coffee in a stylish interior with light, wood-panelled walls.

listings.name: Naked Espresso Bar
listings.content: They claim to specialise in serving and educating their customers all about speciality coffee. Their premium house blend, “Mega Choc” is always on offer, along with a rotating single origin of the day. Also on order are alternative brewing methods such as Aeropress, V60, Syphon and Cold Drip.

listings.name: 65 Degrees
listings.content: The owners have a long history of accolades. Champion barista, world latte artist and award winning coffee blend, gridlock coffee. Fast, friendly service and some of the finest coffee around.

listings.name: The Gin Palace
listings.content: Serious cocktail aficionados should check out this place, for a welcome mix of knowledgeable bartenders, funky bordello ambiance and a laid-back crowd.

listings.name: The Carlton Club
listings.content: Melbourne. Great late night joint or middle of the day, very functional with heaps of little spaces to get cosy and open areas to get your Sunday on. The rooftop bar in up there with the best in town. A must for people coming to Melbourne.

listings.name: The Croft Institute
listings.content: It epitomizes the kitschy-hidden-bar trend of the past few years. Tucked within the narrowest and smelliest alley in Melbourne, this place is somewhat charmingly fitted out like a high school laboratory; complete with beakers, test tubes and retorts. Check out the upstairs 'gymnasium' playing house and electro, and the hospital gurney (with stirrups) on display near the women's toilets.

listings.name: Cookie
listings.content: Excellent bar and cocktails with an upstyle crowd that likes to party hard. Has a restaurant upstairs for dinner serving excellent Thai-inspired meals.

listings.name: Section 8
listings.content: A bar in a car park made from shipping containers. 'Nuff said?

listings.name: Madame Brussels
listings.content: This English Garden party themed bar is on the roof and serves up excellent cocktails by staff in Tennis outfits. Cocktail jugs $30 and $50, 2+ and 4+ serves respectively

listings.name: The Workshop Bar
listings.content: This relaxed bar is in a former motorcycle workshop, hence the name. Run by the same people who run e55.

listings.name: Heartbreaker
listings.content: Bar with an extensive beer list and a solid decor. Also specialises in pizza and with a friendly staff.

listings.name: CityTempo Apartments
listings.content: compact CBD apartments on Queen Street near the Queen Vic Markets. 4 Stars (AAA Tourism), all linen/towels provided with kitchenettes. Some apartments include clothes washer/dryer.

listings.name: Flinders Backpackers
listings.content: 24-hour reception. Centrally located. Twins and doubles have TV. A party hostel, with a nightclub just below the rooms, which will be noisy well into the night. Has many long-term residents, some of who may be unkind to tourists on vacation schedules.
listings.price: 4-bed dorm bed $27/night or $160/week, twin/double $672/night or $439/week, double ensuite $84/night or $499/week

listings.name: Melbourne Central YHA
listings.content: Centrally-located hostel in the backpacker hub of Melbourne. It is situated along the City Circle tram route and most Melbourne attractions are within walking distance. The staff are friendly, helpful and caring. It was opened in 2009 and is highly maintained.
listings.price: Shared room from $33.50, Double $78.50 (YHA members get $3.50 discount)

listings.name: Nomads Melbourne
listings.content: Directly opposite the Queen Victoria Market.
listings.price: Shared dorm from $19, double room from $70

listings.name: Roamer Melbourne
listings.content: Opposite Flinders Street Station, in the centre of Melbourne.Dormitory beds and ensuite private rooms.

listings.name: Atlantis Hotel
listings.content: 24 hour reception

listings.name: Best Western Melbourne City Hotel
listings.content: 24 hour reception.

listings.name: Rydges Melbourne
listings.content: 360 bedroom hotel with Locanda bar and restaurant (mains $27 - 59).

listings.name: Citadines on Bourke Melbourne
listings.content: Apartments available range from studios to two-bedroom executives, and have separate living and dining areas. It also offers a flexible service menu.

listings.name: Rendezvous Hotel Melbourne
listings.content: One of Australia’s finest historic hotels. Built in 1913, this meticulously restored hotel retains the elegant style of the early 1900s while providing you with all the convenience of 21st century technology and amenities. Parking available.

listings.name: The Westin Melbourne
listings.content: Modern, chic and elegantly understated.

listings.name: Park Hyatt
listings.content: Superior service. With Italian marble bathrooms complete with a deep sunken bath with inset TV, twin basins, separate lavatory and therapeutic shower.

listings.name: Grand Hotel Melbourne
listings.content: This heritage-listed apartment hotel has been restored to retain the style of the 1880s while providing guests with modern facilities.

listings.name: Grand Hyatt Melbourne
listings.content: Art Deco style hotel with Veronese marble and international art. All rooms receive access to the Regency Health Club, open daily from 6AM.

listings.name: Hotel Windsor
listings.content: The grand old lady of Melbourne's five-star hotels, and the only surviving grand pre-World War II hotel in Australia. Built in 1883, the Hotel Windsor bills itself as Australia’s only remaining grand hotel. It possesses old world charm with modern luxuries and is opposite Parliament at the top end of Collins St.

listings.name: The Langham Melbourne Hotel
listings.content: The Langham Melbourne hotel offers luxurious Melbourne city accommodation behind the high end Southgate shopping mall, opposite the historic Flinders Street Station. The Langham Melbourne Hotel was the only Australian hotel in Travel and Leisure magazine's list of the world's 100 best hotels (2009). The Langham's Chuan Spa also achieved 'Top Hotel Spa' status in Travel + Leisure USA's 2009 World’s Best Awards readers survey.

listings.name: Clarion Suites Gateway
listings.content: Melbourne CBD hotel which is overlooking the Yarra River and is in the heart of Melbourne’s central business district. All suite and 4,5 stars Melbourne CBD hotel.

listings.name: Quay West Suites Melbourne
listings.content: This Southbank hotel is ideally positioned among Southbank promenade and overlooks the picturesque Yarra River.

listings.name: Treasury on Collins Apartment Hotel
listings.content: On the corner of Queens Street and Collins Street in the heart of Melbourne’s business district. Elegantly restored. this 19th century former bank is now an historic hotel.
